task.title: Unify exact reviewer-to-owner handoff and worker recovery classification

prior_review_verdict.summary: Reject. The first delivery only added "reopen" recognition to canonical_worker_terminal_status without: (1) authenticating the reopen event itself (a missing actor silently passed the truthy-and actor check; a forged/hand-edited event_id was never checked; a worker bound to a stale/superseded task generation still matched on process identity alone), (2) converging worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition -- a status-only shortcut that runs ahead of canonical_worker_terminal_status at both call sites -- onto the same validated proof, and (3)/(4) full real-process race and infra-promotion acceptance. Reproduced with independent in-memory probes; existing green unit suite did not discharge these findings.
prior_review_verdict.response: This delivery fixes (1) and (2) with concrete code changes and new strict-negative/regression tests below, using the reviewer's own probe descriptions as the test list. (3) and (4) remain partially open; see acceptance_matrix_audit for what is and is not covered and why the remainder was not attempted here.

defect_reproduced.description: canonical_worker_terminal_status (the one classifier both poll_workers and boot reconciliation call before recover_lost_worker_lease) only recognized handoff/review_approved/done event types. A committed exact reviewer reopen (which truthfully ends that review attempt and hands in_progress responsibility to the owner) was not in that set, so a truthful post-reopen SIGTERM/exit-143 fell through to generic lost-lease fencing: generation bump, dropped review_requeue_intent, replaced next.
defect_reproduced.reference_example_registry_g19: Registry reviewer run codex-20260906T151222Z-c4a97359 rejected PR5620 head 3f7e9551 at 15:17:07 UTC, generation 19; exact reopen termination at 15:17:18 was followed by lost-lease-bd992815... at 15:17:30, fencing generation 19->20, resolved at 15:17:38 once responsibility was recognized to have moved. See REVIEW_HANDOFF_RECOVERY_RECHECK.md.
defect_reproduced.reference_example_self_task: This task's own PR #5637 reopen by Codex2 at 16:45:14Z (generation 2) was, on the live production command root that predates this fix, fenced by supervisor-worker_lost_lease_recovery_pending at 16:45:47Z (fence_generation 3), then resolved at 16:46:11Z once generic recovery independently recognized responsibility had moved to the owner. Real production reproduction of the identical defect class, captured in ai-activity-log.jsonl.

changes.change: Added "reopen" to the recognized event-type set (now the shared RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES constant) and to the event-type -> valid task-status map (reopen -> {"in_progress"}), gated on expected_role == "reviewer". Fixed the shared actor check so a missing event actor fails closed instead of silently passing (`if event_actor and ...` -> `if not event_actor or ...`). Added, specifically for the reopen path (matching the reviewer's cited lines): a self-consistent event_id check via the existing _ai_status_activity_event_id_matches helper (forged/hand-edited events now rejected); a worker_matches_current_task_generation(worker, task) check (a worker bound to a superseded task generation can no longer pass on process-identity match alone); and a review_requeue_intent cross-check requiring the task's current pending intent to exist, still be status=pending, match the current task_generation, and name the same reviewer/reopened_by as the worker's own identity (a later handoff/reassign/reopen that already cleared or replaced the intent now fails closed).

Converged with canonical_worker_terminal_status instead of remaining a second, weaker classifier. Still accepts a bare lane mismatch (current task status differs from the dispatched role) with zero matching lifecycle events at all, preserving the original historical-dead-PID fallback for a bounded activity-log window. But once a RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES event bound to this exact worker process exists, that event must independently pass canonical_worker_terminal_status's full proof; an event that the strict classifier would reject (forged, unauthenticated, stale-generation, or stale-intent) can no longer still complete the worker through this earlier, weaker call site.

not_changed: _persist_worker_recovery_receipt_locked / _resolve_obsolete_worker_recovery_receipt_locked (generic lost-lease CAS/receipt machinery; still used for genuine crash/expiry/no-transfer cases)
review_decision_intent / review_requeue_intent construction in scripts/ai_status.py command_reopen
active_worker_governance_lease_decision (already reopen-aware for a still-alive worker; unaffected by this change)

reopen_strict_authentication.detail: test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_reopen_strict_negatives (.orchestrator/test_supervisor.py) independently reproduces every probe the reviewer listed against the *previous* delivery and asserts each now returns None: (1) worker bound to task generation 1 replayed against a task already at generation 2; (2) an event missing its actor; (3) a forged event_id (payload changed without recomputing the digest); (4a) task with no review_requeue_intent at all; (4b) a resolved (non-pending) review_requeue_intent; (4c) a review_requeue_intent whose own task_generation no longer matches canonical truth; (4d) a review_requeue_intent naming a different reviewer than the worker's own identity. A baseline fully-authentic case in the same test confirms the positive path still succeeds.

classifier_convergence.detail: worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition no longer accepts a lane mismatch as sufficient proof whenever a matching lifecycle event exists; it now requires that event to pass canonical_worker_terminal_status. test_missing_process_reviewer_with_stale_reopen_still_uses_lost_lease_recovery proves the negative at the poll_workers integration level: a stale-generation reopen event that canonical_worker_terminal_status would reject no longer lets the worker be silently reaped -- recover_lost_worker_lease is called instead. Pre-existing tests test_boot_reconciliation_completes_successful_owner_after_review_handoff and test_successful_dead_owner_after_handoff_reaps_without_lost_lease (no matching event at all, empty activity window) confirm the historical no-event fallback this call site was originally added for still works unchanged.

reproduced_reopen_sequences.detail: test_canonical_worker_terminal_status_recognizes_two_real_recorded_reopens replays two byte-identical rows copied out of the live ai-activity-log.jsonl (not reconstructed/synthetic): REGISTRY-STRATEGY-UNIFIED-CONTRACT-001 generation 19 (event_id ai-status-event-a2440076fb2e5850b45b7dec1d507f3c45af0b3404ae9d619fad005532aa1874, 2026-09-06T15:17:07Z -- Registry g19) and this task's own reopen (event_id ai-status-event-4f20032ba9002383713700fcaa6704e8348a57bda5620bb9deb31073a34b081b, 2026-09-06T16:45:14Z). Each is run twice against the exact real worker/task identity: once through the candidate classifier unmodified (recognizes the reopen, returns in_progress), and once with RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES patched back to the pre-fix set excluding "reopen" (returns None, reproducing the real defect on the same real data). test_missing_process_reviewer_after_exact_reopen_reaps_without_lost_lease additionally reproduces the Registry g19 shape end-to-end through poll_workers with a synthetic-but-fully-authenticated worker/event/intent triple: recover_lost_worker_lease is never called, the worker completes, and task.generation is untouched.

real_two_process_cli_taskstore_outbox_fl.detail: Still not built in this delivery: a genuinely concurrent (separate OS process) reviewer-runner-exits-after-committed-reopen race, and the broader real-process race matrix (reopen/finalize vs recovery/claim/reassign, crash windows around canonical commit/outbox/runner-stop/queue-receipt). What is now covered instead: (a) the classifier fix is proven correct against byte-identical real production activity-log rows (see reproduced_reopen_sequences above), which is real recorded evidence rather than a hand-authored fixture; (b) scripts/test_ai_status.py already exercises command_reopen's two-phase intent protocol, nonce replay, and CLI/git-backed TaskStore commit path extensively (e.g. test_reviewer_reopen_uses_the_same_two_phase_intent_protocol, test_same_second_reopens_receive_distinct_nonce_intents) and is unchanged/reverified by this delivery. Building a new real dual-OS-process race harness spanning both ai_status.py's CLI and supervisor.py's polling loop was judged out of scope for a single classifier-correctness fix given its size and the risk of an unreliable/flaky addition; it should be tracked as explicit follow-up scope (or its own task) rather than attempted piecemeal here.

owner_handoff_approve_reject_done_blocke.detail: Existing supervisor/ai_status suites already cover owner handoff, approve, reopen/reject, done, blocker, and reassignment transitions with strict actor/generation/run/queue/PID-ticks/digest/head negatives (unchanged by this fix; full suite reruns below confirm no regression). This delivery's new coverage is scoped to the reopen-classification path described above; it does not add new coverage for the other listed transitions because their classification paths were not touched.

true_crash_progress_timeout_lease_expiry.detail: recover_lost_worker_lease, review_decision_intent lease-loss handling, and the generic receipt CAS path are untouched by this fix. Full existing regression suites (below) confirm they still fence and recover correctly when no committed reopen/handoff/done/review_approved event matches the worker's exact process identity, and now also when a matching event exists but fails the strict reopen checks (test_missing_process_reviewer_with_stale_reopen_still_uses_lost_lease_recovery).

retirement_of_conflicting_classifiers.detail: The prior delivery's manifest claim that no parallel classifier existed was wrong: worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition ran ahead of canonical_worker_terminal_status at both call sites and could independently complete a worker on lane-mismatch alone, with no event authentication at all. This delivery converges it (see classifier_convergence above) rather than repeating the incorrect claim. active_worker_governance_lease_decision (for a still-alive worker) is a distinct, already-reopen-aware policy for a different question (may this active lease be ended) and remains intentionally separate.

qualification_handoff.detail: Acceptance clause 12 (coordinator-owned qualified runtime promotion and postflight handoff: immutable command/Python identities, unchanged canonical/auth roots and barriers, existing watchdog and one integrator cron, preserved live workers, isolated post-promotion replay and actual dispatch evidence) was not performed. Promoting a new qualified command-root SHA and restarting/replaying against the live supervisor is a high-blast-radius production infrastructure action affecting the shared runtime and all in-flight workers, not a source-review change; it should be executed by Human/Ops (or the existing promotion tooling) after this PR merges, not unilaterally by the implementing worker. The live command root observed at dispatch/review time (65469bc843cab134599995ef7093fe2cf3516af4, then e9d1a1e50b4f098db6e62c1c4e247f1f40f36827 at PR review time) does not yet include this fix; the real self_task defect reproduction above was captured running that pre-fix runtime, which is itself evidence the fix has not yet been activated in production.

verification.collection: Every foreground batch reached a collected terminal exit; no batch was killed or timed out.
verification.development_failures: Fixing the reopen strict-negative checks and classifier convergence initially broke six pre-existing tests that used non-authenticated fixture events (no agent, non-hash event_id, no review_requeue_intent) or relied on worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition's old unconditional lane-mismatch shortcut. Resolved by: (a) making the shared _exact_lifecycle_event test helper stamp a genuine self-consistent event_id and accept an explicit agent, matching ai_status.py's real digest scheme; (b) adding a _pending_review_requeue_intent test helper and wiring it into the affected task fixtures; (c) narrowing worker_completed_after_responsibility_transition's convergence to only require full proof when a matching lifecycle event actually exists, preserving the original no-event historical-dead-PID fallback the two boot-reconciliation tests exercise. All six were reran green; failed attempts are not counted in accepted totals.
